set.body:
Owns fixation-trajectory-evaluation and matched-control-finite-sampling. No random fixation or surface draws are in scope. The title and old uniform hold-last description were misleading.

1. Implement a total time-indexed trajectory evaluator under named clock/unit/endpoint policies, plus checked duration replication. Preserve the pinned reference distinctions: fast sample_fixations uses constant approx(f=0), missing outside its onset range and averaging equal onsets; slow lookup is missing before the first onset, holds the final row after the last onset, and resolves equal onsets to a later row. Neither uses fixation durations to censor gaps. Pin empty/singleton paths, before/at/between/after queries, unsorted query order and repeated times. Native Scanpath's strict ordering must not be weakened just to admit duplicate reference onsets; unsupported/intentional divergence stays explicit. Query cardinality and locations must survive missing support.
2. Pin rep_fixations integer truncation and minimum-one behavior, including 0.29 at resolution 100 versus exact integer-time arithmetic. Name time units and overflow/cardinality failures; do not silently convert requested time precision.
3. Pin finite matched/control candidate construction under recorded R seed/RNGkind: exclude every copy of the true match, retain candidate multiplicity/strata and realized n_perm, cap zero/one/greater-than-pool, duplicates and missing/ambiguous keys. Reuse keyed Selection.BottomK; its cross-language draw differences are intentional, with independent eligible-set/denominator checks, row-order invariance and seed/cap tests. No promise of R PRNG identity.
4. Provide one shared trajectory route for overlap (eyesim-scanpath), density-at-time composition (lookup owned by eyesim-kde) and temporal bins (eyesim-temporal). Joint sample_density(times) evidence must identify both primitives. This task does not duplicate their lookup, spatial-distance or binning implementations.
Evidence gate: use the revision and backend locks in tools/r-parity/baseline.json and r-lock.json; new inputs/manifests are per-ticket, never edits to frozen baseline-cases.json. Record actual exported reference calls, independent analytic expectations, named numerical tolerances and exact identities. Normal workflows/tests require no R; R is an offline fixture oracle only. Exercise public JVM/Scala.js routes, typed failures and declared divergences; keep every failed/missing case. A function name or internal unit test is not cross-library conformance. New published laws require killed mutants. Update case evidence and PARITY.md only after measurement. See docs/TRACKER_REVIEW_2026-09-19.md for shared ownership and closure ordering.
set.title: Pin deterministic trajectories and finite control selection
